mainTopic: Wages and payments involving forbidden or holy items: שביעית produce, סתם יינם, and אתנן paid at a separate time
overview: The amud opens by finishing a משנה (מעשר שני 3:1) about מעשר שני: holy produce may not be given as payment, but it may be given as a free gift. That supports the view that the donkey drivers receive שביעית produce only as a gift. רבא disagrees. He says the drivers' wages really do become holy, as a קנס on people who earn a lot, while a simple worker who earns little was not penalized. Our משנה is strict even with a simple worker because יין נסך is especially severe. The גמרא then asks whether a wage earned working with סתם יינם is also forbidden. It brings רב חסדא, who ordered such a wage of wheat to be burned and buried, and explains why each part of that method is needed. Next comes a story: רבי ינאי's students borrowed שביעית produce from the poor and repaid it in the eighth year, and רבי יוחנן approved. The גמרא compares this to אתנן, rereading a ברייתא to teach that a payment separated in time from the act is not treated as a direct exchange. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a new challenge to that reading, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Holy produce may not be payment, but may be a free gift
steps.stepSummary: The end of a משנה about מעשר שני (מעשר שני 3:1). You may not tell someone to carry your produce to ירושלים in exchange for a share, but you may tell him to bring it there to eat, and people may give each other free gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A person may not say to his friend:] 'Bring these fruits up to ירושלים for me, in return for a share.' But he may say to him: 'Bring them up so we can eat and drink them in ירושלים.' And people may give each other free gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a משנה it began quoting just before this point. It shows that holy produce cannot be used as payment, but it can be given as a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the carrier gets a share as his fee, that counts as doing business with מעשר שני, which is forbidden. If no payment is set up, and the owner simply shares the food or gives a gift, nothing is being 'sold.' This supports the explanation that the donkey drivers can get שביעית produce as a gift, not as wages.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, produce that must be eaten in ירושלים and may not be used for business
To divide, to get a share (here meaning as payment)
A free gift, with nothing expected in return

phrases.english: "Bring these fruits up for me
to Jerusalem, to share [them as my payment],"
but he may say to him:
"Bring them up to eat them and drink them in Jerusalem,"

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹתְנִין זֶה לָזֶה מַתָּנָה שֶׁל חִנָּם.
phrases.english: and they may give one another a free gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַעֲלֵה לִי פֵּירוֹת הַלָּלוּ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם לְחַלֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה brought before this point to support the 'gift' reading of the donkey drivers' payment.
steps.raayaObject: That the drivers' payment of שביעית produce is allowed because it is given as a gift, not as wages.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about מעשר שני distinguishing payment from a free gift.

steps.title: רבא: the drivers' wages are holy; the חכמים penalized them
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the produce paid to the donkey drivers really does carry קדושת שביעית. A worker's wage was not affected because he earns little, but the drivers earn a lot, so the חכמים penalized them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, the wage is holy with the holiness of שביעית. And as for the problem you had from the worker: a worker, whose pay is small, the חכמים did not penalize. Donkey drivers, whose pay is large, the חכמים did penalize.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation from the 'gift' approach that the משנה in step 1 supported. He says the drivers' wages truly become holy, and he answers the challenge that came from the rule about a simple worker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier difficulty was that a worker's wage does not become holy, so why should the drivers' wages? רבא answers that this was a penalty (קנס), and the חכמים only applied it where the earnings are large. So the difference is not about the basic rule, but about who the חכמים chose to penalize.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (the original idea is correct after all)
The holiness of produce from the seventh (שמיטה) year

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rabbinic penalty can depend on practical factors, like how much someone earns, and not only on the basic law.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Actually, it is holy with the holiness of the Sabbatical Year,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the produce the donkey drivers receive as their pay.

phrases.english: and as for what was difficult for you from the worker —
a worker, whose pay is not large,
the Rabbis did not penalize him;
donkey drivers, whose pay is large —
the Rabbis penalized them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם דְּקָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדוּשַּׁת שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'gift' explanation and offers another way to understand the donkey drivers' wages.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on a rabbinic penalty (קנס) tied to the size of the wage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a worker's wage is not holy, the drivers' wage should not be holy either, so it must be a gift.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drivers' wage really is holy, as a קנס that applies only to people who earn a lot.

steps.title: The משנה is strict because יין נסך is especially severe
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains why our משנה forbids even a simple worker's wage when he works with יין נסך: that prohibition is stricter, so it is treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our משנה, which forbids even a worker's wage, is different, because of the strictness of יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers a second problem. If simple workers are not penalized, why does our משנה forbid the wage of someone hired to work with יין נסך?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule from step 2 was that small earners are not penalized. Our משנה seems to penalize a simple worker anyway. רבא says יין נסך is a much harsher prohibition, so there even a small wage is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured as an offering to עבודה זרה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches. The first says the drivers get שביעית produce only as a gift. רבא says it is a real wage that becomes holy as a קנס on big earners. Our משנה's ban on even a simple worker's wage comes from the extra severity of יין נסך.

phrases.english: And our Mishnah —
phrases.notes: The משנה that says if a gentile hired a Jew to work with יין נסך, his wage is forbidden.

phrases.english: the strictness of libation wine is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Heads off a challenge to רבא's distinction, based on our משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה forbids a simple worker's wage, which goes against רבא's rule that small earners were not penalized.
steps.terutzMaskana: יין נסך is so severe that even a small wage is forbidden; that is an exception, not the general rule.

steps.title: Is a wage from working with ordinary gentile wine forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if a Jew is hired to work with סתם יינם, ordinary gentile wine not known to be used for worship, is his wage forbidden like a wage from יין נסך?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If he was hired to work with their ordinary wine, what is the law? Do we say that since its prohibition is as strict as יין נסך, his wage is also forbidden? Or perhaps, since its טומאה is more lenient, its wage is also more lenient?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and gives two possible sides. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סתם יינם is like יין נסך in one way: you may not get any benefit from it. But it is milder in another way: its טומאה is lighter. The question is which comparison decides the law about the wage.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (the חכמים)
Ordinary gentile wine, not known to have been used for worship

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that you may not benefit from סתם יינם itself. The only question here is the worker's wage.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If he was hired for their ordinary wine, what is the law?
Do we say:
since its prohibition is as severe as libation wine —
his wage is also forbidden;
or perhaps:
since its impurity is lighter —
phrases.notes: Some versions say קיל, in round brackets; the corrected wording is קִילָא, in square brackets. Both mean 'light.'

phrases.english: its wage is also lighter?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שְׂכָרוֹ לִסְתָם יֵינָן, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea from step 3 that יין נסך is especially strict, and asks whether סתם יינם shares that strictness for wages.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the wage for working with סתם יינם is forbidden like the wage from יין נסך.

steps.title: רב חסדא orders the wheat burned and buried
steps.stepSummary: A man rented out his ship to carry סתם יינם and was paid in wheat. רב חסדא told him to burn it and bury it in a graveyard, which suggests the wage is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A certain man rented out his ship to carry their ordinary wine, and they paid him wheat as his fee. He came before רב חסדא, who told him: Go burn it and bury it in a graveyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to try to answer the question from step 4. רב חסדא treated the wage as fully forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning and burying is how one gets rid of something you may not benefit from at all. So רב חסדא seems to hold that a wage from סתם יינם is forbidden, just like a wage from יין נסך.
steps.whatToRemember: The question was whether a wage from סתם יינם is forbidden. רב חסדא's ruling suggests that it is.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that a certain man rented out his ship
for their ordinary wine;
they gave him wheat as payment.
He came before Rav Ḥisda.
He said to him:
Go burn them and bury them in a graveyard.
phrases.notes: Some versions say בקברי, in round brackets; the corrected wording is בֵּי קִבְרֵי, in square brackets. Either way it means a cemetery.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאֹגַר אַרְבֵּיהּ לִסְתָם יֵינָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question of step 4 with a practical ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That a wage from working with סתם יינם is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story in which רב חסדא ordered wheat paid for carrying סתם יינם to be burned and buried.

steps.title: Why not just scatter the wheat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא did not simply tell the ship owner to scatter the forbidden wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him tell him: scatter it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב חסדא's method. Burning and burying is a lot of work, so why not just scatter the wheat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that the wage is forbidden is not being challenged here, only the method of getting rid of it. If scattering is enough, the extra steps seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him (a standard way of suggesting a simpler option)

phrases.english: But let him say to him: Scatter them!
phrases.notes: "Them" means the wheat kernels the ship owner was paid with in Step 5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method in רב חסדא's ruling from Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's instruction to burn the wheat and bury it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler way to get rid of the wheat is available, so the burning and burying seem unnecessary.

steps.title: Scattered kernels could cause a mishap
steps.stepSummary: Scattering is not enough, because people might find the kernels and eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would come to a mishap through them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that scattered wheat is still usable. Someone could gather it and come to use forbidden food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scattering only moves the wheat around. Since the kernels stay whole and edible, the danger of someone using them remains.

keyTerms.meaning: A mishap, meaning someone accidentally doing something forbidden

phrases.english: People will come through them to a mishap.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical concern that justifies the stricter method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Scattering would be enough to get rid of the wheat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Scattered whole kernels could be picked up and used, so scattering alone is not enough.

steps.title: Then burn it and scatter the ashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: then burn the wheat and scatter it. Why bury it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him burn them and scatter them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the wheat must be burned. Now it asks why scattering the ashes would not be enough without burying them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning solves the problem from Step 7, since nobody can eat ashes. So the burial step now looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: But let him burn them and scatter them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of Step 7 and challenges the burial part of the method
steps.kashyaTarget: The burial part of רב חסדא's instruction
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the wheat is burned it cannot be eaten, so scattering the ashes should be enough.

steps.title: The ashes might be used as fertilizer
steps.stepSummary: Scattered ashes could still be used to fertilize fields, so they must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps they will fertilize with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ashes are still useful as fertilizer. Burying them makes sure nobody gets any benefit from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is not only eating. Any benefit from this forbidden wage is a problem, and fertilizing a field is a benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: They fertilize (from זֶבֶל, manure or fertilizer)

phrases.english: Perhaps people will fertilize with them.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burned ashes can simply be scattered.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ashes can still be used as fertilizer, so they must be buried.

steps.title: Why not bury the wheat whole, like execution tools?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the wheat must be burned at all, since execution tools are buried whole with the executed person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him bury them as they are! Did we not learn: the stone a person was stoned with, the tree he was hung on, the sword he was killed with, and the scarf he was strangled with are all buried with him?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the burning step. It brings a source showing that forbidden objects can be buried whole without being burned first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Execution tools are forbidden for benefit, yet the source says only to bury them, not burn them. So for forbidden wheat, burial alone should also be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: In their original form, as they are
Did we not learn? (introduces a taught source as a challenge)
Was stoned (סְקִילָה, the death penalty of stoning)

phrases.english: But let him bury them as they are!
Did we not learn:
Both the stone with which he was stoned,
and the tree on which he was hung,
and the sword with which he was killed,
and the scarf with which he was strangled —
all of them are buried with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the wheat must be buried and now challenges the burning step, using a taught source
steps.kashyaTarget: The burning part of רב חסדא's instruction
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Execution tools are forbidden for benefit and are only buried, not burned, so the wheat should be treated the same way.

steps.title: A court graveyard makes it obvious, a random burial does not
steps.stepSummary: Execution tools buried in the court's graveyard are clearly known as forbidden. Buried wheat might be mistaken for stolen goods someone hid, so it must be burned first.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since they bury them in the court's graveyard, it is clear that these belong to people executed by the court. Here it is not clear. One might say: someone stole this and brought it and buried it here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing a difference between the two cases. With execution tools everyone knows they are forbidden, but with buried wheat a person might think it is just hidden stolen food and dig it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burial alone works only when the place itself shows the object is forbidden. Buried wheat gives no such sign, so it must be burned first to make it useless.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter is evident, it is clear to everyone

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's "burn and bury" is not extra strictness. Each step blocks a real way the forbidden wheat could still be used: whole kernels can be eaten, ashes can fertilize, and buried whole wheat might be dug up as "hidden stolen goods."

phrases.english: There, since they bury them in the court's place,
the matter is evident
that these belong to those executed by the court.
Here, the matter is not evident;
one might say: a person stole it
and brought it and buried it here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10 by showing how the two cases differ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Like execution tools, the wheat could be buried whole.
steps.terutzMaskana: Execution tools are clearly known as forbidden because of where they are buried. Buried wheat is not, so it must be burned first.

steps.title: רבי ינאי's students borrow שביעית produce from the poor
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי's students borrowed שביעית produce from poor people and paid it back in the eighth year. רבי יוחנן said they acted properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The students of רבי ינאי borrowed שביעית produce from poor people and paid them back in the eighth year. People came and told רבי יוחנן. He said to them: They are acting properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a story about שביעית produce. רבי יוחנן approves of borrowing it and paying it back later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people who reported this seem to have worried that paying back שביעית produce was a forbidden kind of trading with it. רבי יוחנן's answer shows that a loan repaid in the eighth year is acceptable, though the גמרא does not yet explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the seventh (שְׁמִיטָּה) year, which has special holiness
The eighth year, the year after שְׁמִיטָּה

phrases.english: Those of the house of Rabbi Yannai would borrow
seventh-year produce from poor people,
and repay them in the eighth year.
They came and told this to Rabbi Yoḥanan.
He said to them: They are acting properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי יָזְפִי פֵּירֵי שְׁבִיעִית מֵעֲנִיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of סתם יינם and opens a new section about שביעית produce
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowing שביעית produce from the poor and repaying it in the eighth year is proper, according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The parallel case: payment to a זונה is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the matching case in אתנן is also permitted, and brings a ברייתא to show it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the matching case of a זונה's payment, it is permitted. As a ברייתא teaches: if he gave her payment and did not have relations with her, or had relations with her and did not give her payment, her payment is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the borrowing case to a parallel case in the laws of אתנן. It quotes a ברייתא to show that this kind of payment is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids offering an animal given as a זונה's payment. Just as paying later for borrowed שביעית produce does not count as trading, a payment that is not directly tied to the act does not count as אתנן. The ברייתא's exact wording will be questioned in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given to a זונה. An animal given this way may not be brought as a קרבן.
And the case that matches them

phrases.english: And in the corresponding case of a prostitute's payment, it is permitted,
phrases.notes: This matches the previous case of רבי ינאי's students paying back שביעית produce later. On אתנן, see דברים 23:19.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: נָתַן לָהּ וְלֹא בָּא עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: as it is taught: if he gave her payment but did not have relations with her,
or he had relations with her but did not give her payment,
her payment is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a parallel from אתנן to the ruling that paying back שביעית produce later is acceptable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case that parallels the borrowing case, a זונה's payment is permitted for a קרבן, as the ברייתא states.

steps.title: The first case in the ברייתא seems too obvious
steps.stepSummary: If he paid and never had relations with her, of course it is permitted. It is just a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave her payment and did not have relations with her, that is obvious! Since he did not have relations with her, it is simply a gift he gave her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first case in the ברייתא. Why would anyone need to be told it is permitted?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something only becomes אתנן because it is payment for relations. With no relations at all, the item is just an ordinary present, so the ברייתא seems to be teaching nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לָהּ וְלֹא בָּא עָלֶיהָ — פְּשִׁיטָא,
phrases.english: He gave her but did not have relations with her? That is obvious,
since he did not have relations with her,
it is merely a gift that he gave her!

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן לָהּ וְלֹא בָּא עָלֶיהָ פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first case of the ברייתא quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's first case: he gave her payment but had no relations with her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without relations there is no payment for anything, so it is clearly just a gift. The ruling seems pointless.

steps.title: The second case in the ברייתא makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: If he never paid her, what payment is there to permit?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: if he had relations with her and did not give her anything, then he gave her nothing at all. Since he did not give her anything, what does 'her payment is permitted' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second problem with the ברייתא. The second case talks about permitting a payment that does not exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the ruling is obvious. In the second case, it seems to have no subject at all, because nothing was given. Together, these problems push the גמרא to reread the ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ, בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְלֹא נָתַן לָהּ —
phrases.english: And furthermore, he had relations with her but did not give her payment:

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא יָהֵיב לָהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: he did not give her anything at all,
and since he did not give her anything,
what does 'her payment is permitted' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְלֹא נָתַן לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate challenge to the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's second case: he had relations with her but gave her nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no payment to permit, so the ruling 'her payment is permitted' has nothing to apply to.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: payment separated from the act by time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means the payment came before or after the act with time in between, so it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: if he gave her payment and afterwards had relations with her, or had relations with her and afterwards gave her payment, her payment is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both problems by reading the ברייתא differently. 'Did not' really means 'not at the same time.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both cases make sense. A real payment was given, and real relations took place. Because the two were separated by time, the payment does not count as אתנן. This matches the borrowing case, where paying later is not treated as trading in שביעית produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it means

steps.whatToRemember: When a payment is separated in time from what it pays for, it is not treated as a direct exchange. This is true for אתנן, and also for repaying borrowed שביעית produce.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: he gave her payment and afterwards had relations with her,
phrases.notes: 'Afterwards' means some time later, not right away. That gap is the whole point.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָתַן לָהּ —
phrases.english: or he had relations with her and afterwards gave her payment,
her payment is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves both challenges by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא meant there was no payment at all, or no relations at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both payment and relations happened, but with time between them, so the payment is not אתנן.

steps.title: Starting a question on the first case of the new reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to question the case where he paid first and had relations later.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave her payment and afterwards had relations with her, then when he has relations with her...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next challenge to the new reading. The question is not finished here and continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא focuses on paying first and having relations later. It is beginning to ask what happens at the moment of relations, when the earlier payment may become tied to the act.

steps.kashyaTarget: The case where he gave payment first and had relations later.
